Seattle and Eastside kitchens

Kitchen remodeling for Seattle and Eastside homes, planned from Redmond

RT Signature Homes approaches kitchen remodeling as a balance of circulation, storage, work zones, lighting, materials, and construction reality. For homes in Seattle, Redmond, Bellevue, Kirkland, and nearby Eastside neighborhoods, those decisions also have to fit occupied houses, constrained access, and the city that will review the work.

Request a consultation Explore design ideas
Call (206) 407-6291
Completed RT project photography · Redmond

Every visible finish depends on decisions behind the walls and inside the cabinets. We plan those from our Redmond office as one design-build path, not as a finish package handed from one vendor to the next.

Project fit

A strong fit includes full kitchen renovations, layout changes, cabinet replacement, island redesign, and projects that require several trades to work in a precise sequence.

Typical scope

  • Kitchen layout and circulation planning
  • Cabinetry, storage, island, and millwork coordination
  • Countertops, backsplash, flooring, and paint
  • Lighting, appliance, plumbing, ventilation, and electrical coordination
  • Protection, temporary-use planning, and final detailing
  • Sequencing around an occupied Seattle or Eastside home

Design ideas

Kitchen remodeling inspiration

Explore visual directions alongside the planning, material, and performance decisions that help turn an idea into a buildable project.

Kitchen design ideas

The strongest kitchens balance work zones, circulation, storage, daylight, task lighting, and materials that can handle daily use. This gallery focuses on combinations that feel refined without sacrificing function.

Explore the gallery

Build storage around real routines.

Cabinet layouts should respond to how the household cooks, unloads groceries, entertains, cleans, and stores small appliances.

Door clearances, fillers, appliance specifications, and hardware are resolved before orders are released. Eastside kitchens often share walls with living rooms, mudrooms, and hallways that already have their own finish language. We keep cabinetry, counters, and adjacent rooms on the same plan.

Make circulation, work surfaces, and light support one another.

Islands and work zones need adequate clearance, useful task lighting, and realistic relationships to appliances and seating.

The design should remain comfortable when more than one person is using the room. In Seattle and Eastside houses, daylight, window placement, and how the kitchen meets the rest of the floor plan often decide the layout before a style board does.

Seattle, Redmond, and Bellevue review kitchen work differently. If the kitchen moves plumbing, electrical, or structure, the city that has jurisdiction typically requires a residential building permit. Cosmetic swaps in place may not. We confirm the pathway by address. For how Redmond publishes building-permit fees by valuation, see What remodel permits can cost in Redmond. That table is a city schedule, not a bid, and it is not the fee schedule for Seattle or Bellevue.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written. On the Eastside that usually includes access, occupancy, and which municipality will issue the permit.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Project size, layout changes, and finish level
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements for the applicable city
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, weather, and project sequencing in an occupied home

Questions homeowners ask

Kitchen remodeling FAQs

Can the kitchen layout be changed?

Often, but plumbing, ventilation, structure, windows, electrical capacity, and adjacent-room circulation all affect what is practical.

When should cabinets and appliances be selected?

Early enough that dimensions, utilities, ventilation, and lead times can be coordinated before construction sequencing is finalized.

Do you have a Redmond showroom kitchen?

No. The office is in Redmond at 4164 148th Ave NE. Work is planned around your house. Design galleries are inspiration, not a showroom of completed RT kitchens.

Will the first conversation give me a kitchen price?

Complex residential work needs the property, existing conditions, scope, and selections before a responsible recommendation.

Can you remodel only the kitchen?

Yes, when the scope is a fit. We still look at how the kitchen meets the rest of the home.
